program.source: export function evaluate({ inputs, time, seed, state }) { const launchSpeed = inputs.launchSpeed; const gravity = inputs.gravity; const apexTime = launchSpeed / gravity; const apexHeight = (launchSpeed * launchSpeed) / (2 * gravity); const t = time; const tossedVelocity = launchSpeed - gravity * t; const tossedAcceleration = -gravity; const tossedHeight = launchSpeed * t - 0.5 * gravity * t * t; const isAtTop = t >= apexTime; const dropVelocity = isAtTop ? -gravity * (t - apexTime) : 0; const dropAcceleration = isAtTop ? -gravity : 0; const dropHeight = isAtTop ? apexHeight - 0.5 * gravity * Math.pow(t - apexTime, 2) : apexHeight; const heightScale = 120; const baseY = 360; const tossX = 180; const dropX = 460; const laneWidth = 240; const laneHeight = 320; const getScreenY = (h) => baseY - (h / 2.2) * laneHeight; const tossScreenY = getScreenY(Math.max(0, Math.min(2.2, tossedHeight))); const dropScreenY = getScreenY(Math.max(0, Math.min(2.2, dropHeight))); let tossState = "Rising"; if (t < 0.05) tossState = "At launch"; else if (Math.abs(t - apexTime) < 0.05) tossState = "At the top"; else if (t > apexTime && tossScreenY < baseY) tossState = "Falling"; else if (t >= apexTime && tossedHeight <= 0) tossState = "At launch height"; let dropState = "Held in place"; if (t > apexTime && t < apexTime + 0.05) dropState = "Just released"; else if (t >= apexTime + 0.05 && dropHeight > 0) dropState = "Falling together"; else if (t >= apexTime && dropHeight <= 0) dropState = "At launch height"; const objects = []; objects.push(...sdk.panel({ x: 50, y: 40, w: laneWidth, h: laneHeight, title: "Toss lane", state: tossState, id: "lane.toss" })); objects.push(...sdk.panel({ x: 350, y: 40, w: laneWidth, h: laneHeight, title: "Drop lane", state: dropState, id: "lane.drop" })); objects.push(sdk.circle("ball.toss", tossX, tossScreenY, 28, { role: "output" })); objects.push(sdk.circle("ball.drop", dropX, dropScreenY, 28, { role: "output" })); objects.push(...sdk.vector("vec.v.toss", { x: tossX - 20, y: tossScreenY }, { value: tossedVelocity, direction: "up" }, { scale: 15, label: "v" })); objects.push(...sdk.vector("vec.a.toss", { x: tossX + 20, y: tossScreenY }, { value: tossedAcceleration, direction: "up" }, { scale: 15, label: "a" })); objects.push(...sdk.vector("vec.v.drop", { x: dropX - 20, y: dropScreenY }, { value: dropVelocity, direction: "up" }, { scale: 15, label: "v" })); objects.push(...sdk.vector("vec.a.drop", { x: dropX + 20, y: dropScreenY }, { value: dropAcceleration, direction: "up" }, { scale: 15, label: "a" })); objects.push(...sdk.callout(tossX + 45, tossScreenY - 20, ["v: " + sdk.format(tossedVelocity, 2) + " m/s", "a: " + sdk.format(tossedAcceleration, 2) + " m/s^2"], { id: "callout.toss" })); objects.push(...sdk.callout(dropX + 45, dropScreenY - 20, ["v: " + sdk.format(dropVelocity, 2) + " m/s", "a: " + sdk.format(dropAcceleration, 2) + " m/s^2"], { id: "callout.drop" })); objects.push(sdk.gate("gate", dropX, getScreenY(apexHeight), { open: isAtTop, label: "Apex Gate" })); objects.push(sdk.axis("axis.toss", { x: tossX - 100, y: baseY, length: laneHeight, orientation: "y", min: 0, max: 2.2, label: "Height", unit: "m" })); objects.push(sdk.axis("axis.drop", { x: dropX - 100, y: baseY, length: laneHeight, orientation: "y", min: 0, max: 2.2, label: "Height", unit: "m" })); return { frame: { width: 640, height: 420, objects: objects, readouts: [{ id: "tossedVelocity", value: tossedVelocity }, { id: "tossedAcceleration", value: tossedAcceleration }, { id: "dropVelocity", value: dropVelocity }, { id: "dropAcceleration", value: dropAcceleration }] }, quantities: { launchSpeed: launchSpeed, gravity: gravity, apexTime: apexTime, apexHeight: apexHeight, tossedVelocity: tossedVelocity, tossedAcceleration: tossedAcceleration, tossedHeight: tossedHeight, dropVelocity: dropVelocity, dropAcceleration: dropAcceleration, dropHeight: dropHeight } }; }

manifest.title: Zero velocity isn’t zero acceleration.
manifest.summary: Compare a tossed ball with a ball dropped from rest at the apex to see why acceleration remains nonzero when velocity is zero.
manifest.description: Two side-by-side lanes show a tossed ball and a dropped ball. At the top of the toss, velocity is zero while acceleration remains equal to negative gravity, and a gate releases the second ball.
manifest.instructions: Change launch speed or gravity, then press Play. At each pause, compare velocity and acceleration.
